why: Rule 6: at the end of a commitment span an AI keeps its opponent unless another is MATERIALLY better. A negative margin makes any improvement sufficient, so the AI flips target at every span boundary -- the per-tick-thrashing failure mode one span removed. Worth an entry because the first version of the matching test could not detect it: its challenger was further from preferred range than the held target, so no margin was ever crossed.
killedBy: committed opponent selection does not switch at expiry for a trivially better candidate, but does for a material one
